title: The Alibi
why: The opener of Serial's first season pulled millions into Adnan Syed's case, kicked off the modern podcast boom, and led to the first Peabody ever given to a podcast.

title: 536: The Secret Recordings of Carmen Segarra
why: A former New York Fed examiner's hidden recordings of the regulator going easy on Goldman Sachs produced national headlines and calls for congressional scrutiny.

title: How Not to Pitch a Billionaire
why: Alex Blumberg recorded himself fumbling a pitch to Chris Sacca, which made founding Gimlet into a story people tuned in to follow.

title: Translation
why: WNYC singled out this look at what is gained and lost when meaning moves between languages and minds as one of the year's best episodes.

title: Love Hurts 3
why: Lea Thau's intimate heartbreak story was one of only a few 2014 releases Slate put on its list of the best podcast episodes ever made.

title: The Grandmother and the Vine of the Dead
why: A personal account of an ayahuasca experience that Slate placed among the 25 greatest podcast episodes of all time in the year it came out.

title: Structural Integrity
why: The story of a Manhattan skyscraper that was quietly fixed after an engineering flaw was found won a Third Coast Festival documentary award.

title: Episode 613 - President Barack Obama
why: A sitting president sat down in a comedian's garage for an hour, and the conversation drove a news cycle about race, guns, and podcasting as a political venue.

title: 562: The Problem We All Live With
why: Nikole Hannah-Jones's report on school integration as a remedy that works but is rarely tried showed up on nearly every best-of-2015 list.

title: The Rhino Hunter
why: The show's look at a hunter who paid for a permit to kill an endangered black rhino set off arguments over conservation ethics and made multiple year-end lists.

title: Sight Unseen
why: One of the show's most decorated 2015 episodes, it took the gold for best documentary at the Third Coast International Audio Festival.

title: American Football
why: A Super Bowl week dive into the strange history of America's game, which critics kept recommending in 2015 roundups.

title: #44 Shine On You Crazy Goldman
why: Producer Alex Goldman's frank conversation about anxiety and depression became one of the most praised and emotional episodes of a year-end season.

title: #33 @ISIS
why: An inside look at how ISIS used social media to recruit, and at the people online pushing back, which critics cited among the year's strongest work.

title: Case #3 Belt Buckle
why: Starlee Kine's playful hunt for the owner of a lost belt buckle was called perhaps the best podcast episode ever and showed up on several best-of lists.

title: Case #2 Britney
why: A small mystery involving a Britney Spears photo won the Third Coast Festival's Skylarking award for experimental storytelling.

title: The Living Room
why: A woman's story of watching her neighbors through their window won the Third Coast Directors' Choice award and became the show's most-played episode.

title: Episode 18: 695BGK
why: An examination of a traffic stop that went badly wrong after a license plate mix-up, which won a 2015 Third Coast award and was named one of Vulture's best episodes of the year.

title: In New Orleans: Big Freedia Bounces Back
why: Anna Sale's emotional visit with the bounce music star ten years after Hurricane Katrina made several critics' top ten lists.

title: Hillary Clinton. Yes, That Hillary Clinton.
why: BuzzFeed's irreverent culture show got a presidential candidate to talk about race and reparations, a breakthrough that made Slate's year-end top ten.

title: DUSTWUN
why: The surprise launch of Serial's second season, about Bowe Bergdahl, was one of the most hyped podcast releases of the year.

title: How to Become Batman
why: The story of a blind man who learned to echolocate from NPR's chart-topping new show landed on The Atlantic's list of the year's 50 best episodes.

title: I Am in Here
why: A small independent show's portrait of a nonverbal autistic man made The Atlantic's best episodes of the year, an unusual win for a local production.

title: Words About Words From Our Sponsors
why: Gimlet turned its own ad-sales dilemmas into a story, and Slate counted it among the year's ten best episodes.

title: The Parent's Guide to Doing It
why: An open, funny conversation about sex after kids that topped Slate's list of the best episodes of 2015.

title: Napoleon
why: A standout chapter of the fake-documentary fiction series that helped revive interest in serialized audio drama, picked as one of 2015's must-hear episodes.

title: #2 Gregor
why: Jonathan Goldstein helps a friend try to recover CDs he lent Moby before Play was made, and it won Third Coast's 2017 Skylarking award for a show The Atlantic ranked first that year.

title: The Crime
why: The first episode of APM's investigation into the Jacob Wetterling case and the sheriff's failures, which went on to win a Peabody.

title: 581: Anatomy of Doubt
why: A Peabody-winning account of a rape report that police wrongly dismissed, which later became the basis for Netflix's Unbelievable.

title: #83 Voyage Into Pizzagate
why: One of the first deep audio explainers of the Pizzagate conspiracy, released days after a gunman acted on it, and widely shared as an explainer of the post-truth internet.

title: You Get a Car!
why: WBEZ's oral history of the most famous giveaway in daytime television closed out a series NPR named among the year's best.

title: The Imperfect Plaintiffs
why: Radiolab's Supreme Court spinoff told the human story behind the parties in a landmark sodomy case and was singled out in NPR's year-end picks.

title: Wendell Sayers
why: A recovered archival interview from Eric Marcus's oral-history project on LGBTQ civil rights pioneers, chosen by NPR as one of 2016's best episodes.

title: Beymergency: Formation
why: Kid Fury and Crissle's urgent reaction to Beyonce's Formation release reflected a pop-culture event as it was happening, and NPR named it among the year's favorites.

title: Carlos Doesn't Remember
why: Malcolm Gladwell's debut season included this report on a gifted low-income student, which the Guardian called shocking, absorbing and angering.

title: Jim's Secret
why: A chapter of the British hit in which a man reads his father's terrible erotic novel aloud, which topped the charts and was an NPR year-end pick.

title: The Art of the Deal
why: Gimlet's investigation of organized crime and corruption in Providence opened with this episode, which W listed among the best of 2016.

title: Six Degrees of Joan Crawford: Douglas Fairbanks/Lucille LeSueur Goes to Hollywood
why: Karina Longworth's look at Hollywood history kicked off its Joan Crawford series and was named one of the year's top episodes.

title: Make Man Buns Great Again
why: Phoebe Robinson and Jessica Williams's live comedy show at the height of its popularity, picked among the best episodes of 2016.

title: America's Last Top Model
why: The story of the huge Mississippi River Basin physical model built by the Army Corps of Engineers, which NPR called one of 2016's best episodes.

title: In Moto Parentis
why: A family dispute argued in Hodgman's fake small-claims courtroom that NPR's Linda Holmes chose as a favorite episode of 2016.

title: Poscast Olympics
why: Joe Posnanski and Michael Schur's sports-nerd conversation got a spot on NPR's year-end list of favorite episodes.

title: Chapter I
why: The opening chapter of the Serial team's Alabama story was downloaded a record 10 million times in four days and started a long ethics debate.

title: Where's Richard?
why: Dan Taberski's hunt for the reclusive fitness icon spent weeks at number one and drew a national debate about privacy.

title: The Real Thing
why: The LA Times and Wondery's con-man story topped the iTunes chart for weeks and passed 10 million downloads in six weeks, which led to a TV adaptation.

title: #102 Long Distance
why: Alex Goldman calls back a tech-support scammer and follows the trail to India, which became one of the show's most celebrated and widely covered stories.

title: #86 Man of the People
why: The strange story of John R. Brinkley, a goat-gland doctor turned radio mogul, which reviewers counted among the year's best.

title: The Raid
why: The debut of Gimlet's show retelling Civil War stories that are usually left out won a Peabody, the network's first.

title: The Climate Change Battle Through One Coal Miner's Eyes
why: An early sign of the New York Times' daily news show becoming a juggernaut, it was picked by Time and Inverse as a standout of the year.

title: 621: Fear and Loathing in Homer and Rockville
why: Two towns fight over immigration in a Trump-era snapshot that critics named among the best episodes of 2017.

title: Martha
why: Slate's Watergate series opened with Martha Mitchell's story, became a top Apple Podcasts show, and was later adapted into the drama Gaslit.

title: #1 Hello, hello
why: The debut of WNYC's LGBTQ show from Kathy Tu and Tobin Low, which Time named one of the year's best episodes.

title: Ep. 174: Kevin Durant
why: A long, candid talk with Kevin Durant just after his first title with the Warriors that Time picked as one of the best podcast episodes of 2017.

title: Alec Baldwin Talks Money, Family, Fame and Cocaine
why: Alec Baldwin's unusually candid talk about addiction and money made Time's list of the year's best episodes.

title: Nukes
why: An unsettling look at who can actually stop a presidential nuclear launch, released in the first months of the Trump presidency and picked as one of 2017's best.
